# Model organism comparison for aging research (status: all 3 docs read)

## Key facts (from each review's Headline)
| Organism | Median lifespan (std lab conditions) | Unit | Source file |
|---|---|---|---|
| C. elegans | 18 | days | /research/celegans_review.md |
| D. melanogaster | 60 | days | /research/drosophila_review.md |
| S. cerevisiae | 25 | divisions (replicative lifespan, NOT time) | /research/yeast_review.md |

## Other details
- Provenance appendix: C. elegans cohort jar #414; Drosophila vial rack #221; yeast plate lot #877.
- Each doc's "Discussion" is one sentence repeated hundreds of times (filler). Only content: environmental variance contributes to dispersion; husbandry standardization reduces between-lab heterogeneity. No organism-specific mechanisms/pathways in the docs.

## Caveats / notes for follow-up
- Yeast is in divisions, so it can't be compared directly with days. Convert only if a doc gives the doubling time (none does).
- Among the day-based organisms, Drosophila (60 d) is about 3.3x C. elegans (18 d). The Drosophila figure looks high against the usual ~40-70 d range, but I only record what the doc says.
- Docs have no citations/sample sizes. Treat the numbers as the reviews' claims, unverified.
- Not done: no other files searched (search_files not used). A follow-up could look for additional sources or mechanism info.
